Who can I tell about bullying?

explain.say: If someone is bullying you, the first thing to know is on the board in big letters: it is not your fault. Nobody deserves to be bullied. You are not alone, and there are people who can help.

explain.say: In the moment, stay as calm as you can and walk away towards people and adults. If it feels safe, say firmly: stop, I do not like that. Look at those steps. Can you practise saying it?

explain.say: This is the most important step: tell a trusted adult, and keep telling until it stops. Telling is not telling tales. It is getting help. Who would you tell first?

explain.say: Keeping a record helps too: write what happened and when, or save screenshots of messages. And stay near friends, because bullies often pick on people who are alone. See the ticks?

explain.say: Look at all the people around you: a parent or carer, a teacher, a school counsellor, a grandparent or aunt, and a child helpline. You did really well learning this. You always have someone to turn to.

faq.q: Is it my fault I am being bullied?
faq.a: No, never. Bullying is a choice the other person makes. There is nothing wrong with you.
asks: Tell me about the It is not your fault

faq.q: Who can I tell if I am being bullied?
faq.a: A parent or carer, a teacher, a school counsellor, a grandparent, aunt or uncle, or a child helpline. If one adult does not help, tell another until someone does.
asks: Tell me about the Tell a trusted adult

faq.a: A free phone or chat service where trained people listen to children and help them. Many countries have one, like Childline 0800 1111 in the UK and 1098 in India.
asks: Tell me about the Child helpline

faq.q: What if telling makes it worse?
faq.a: That is a common worry. Adults can help in ways that keep you safe, and schools have rules to stop bullying. Tell an adult about your worry too.
asks: Will the bully find out I told?

faq.a: No. Fighting can get you hurt or in trouble. Walking away, saying stop and telling an adult are safer and work better.

facts: Child Helpline International links free helplines for children in more than 130 countries.
Childline in the UK (0800 1111) and Childline India (1098) are free numbers for children who need help.

quiz.why: Adults can step in and stop bullying, so telling is key.

wrong.0: Keeping it secret lets it go on.

quiz.say: You told a teacher, but nothing changed. What now?

options.show: Tell another trusted adult, like a parent or counsellor
options.say: Tell another trusted adult, like a parent or counsellor

quiz.why: Keep telling until someone helps. You deserve to be safe.

wrong.0: Do not give up; there are other adults who can help.
